headline: Committee discusses Act 171 transition to Maui County, defers the item

meeting.body: Maui County Council Kōmike Aloha ʻĀina
meeting.voteItem: Designate the introduced individuals as resource persons under Rule 18A
meeting.summary: The chair said Senate Bill 1432 became Act 171 on June 26, 2026, and Maui County takes over the area one year after the last patient leaves. Oral public testimony was closed and the item was deferred.
meeting.recap: The chair said Senate Bill 1432 became Act 171 on June 26, 2026.[[0:04:42]] The law starts after the last patient leaves; one year later, Maui County takes over the area.[[0:04:48]] The chair formed a community advisory group, or hui, which has met three times.[[0:07:46]] He said special peninsula fishing rules will end after the transition; statewide rules will still apply.[[0:52:46]] The chair said the state asked Maui County to step in because no local government would remain.[[2:09:45]] The chair is considering exempting vehicles there for now.[[3:05:07]]
decided: No one objected, so the invited speakers were named resource persons (people who can answer the committee's questions).
No one objected, so oral public testimony was closed.
No one objected, so the item was deferred.
meeting.next: The state's aquatic resources division plans to write place-based rules for the peninsula but has not started. A committee member asked staff to send the managing director a written question on the county's preparation for the transition. The chair said Molokaʻi Community Plan changes would come after the last patient, going to the council and the Molokaʻi Planning Commission.
